raw_response:
I am 67 years old. No schooling, but 46 years on this land in Quzhou. My farm is 10.9 mu, all cotton. Just me and my husband now — two mouths, four hands, getting slower every year.

I don't read books and I don't trust newfangled ideas. I trust what I've seen with my own eyes. Last year I got about 500 jin of lint per mu — about 250 kg for those who count that way. This year I'll do the same as always, though maybe a little less fertilizer if the shop prices are still high. Money doesn't grow on trees, and my pocket is small.

Late April, when the soil feels warm under my bare feet, I'll plant. I buy the improved hybrid seeds from the county shop — costs me about 50 yuan per mu. Before that, I hire Old Zhang's tractor to plow in early April. Then me and my old man lay the plastic mulch by hand. It's backbreaking, but it keeps the weeds down and the soil warm, and at 67 I can't afford to hoe all summer.

For fertilizer, I put down almost a full bag of that three-in-one compound fertilizer per mu before planting — about 80 jin, because a full 100-jin bag is too expensive this year. Then when the cotton starts flowering in mid-July, I spread about 25 jin of urea per mu. My neighbor uses more, but last year I cut back a little and the yield was still fine. Why waste money? Better to have cash in hand for medicine or emergencies than to pour it all into the field.

Irrigate twice from the well. Pumping costs electricity, so I only do it when I have to — once when the flowers are blooming and it's hot as an oven in July, and once in August if the sky stays dry. If the rains come, maybe only once. I watch the clouds like my mother taught me. Water is precious, and I won't spend yuan on the pump unless the plants are thirsty.

For bugs, I walk the fields every morning with my tea. If I see bollworms or the leaves look chewed, I spray. I also use herbicide because at 67, bending down to weed all day would break my back. I can't afford to let the weeds win, but I can't afford a bad back either.

Picking is what kills us. Cotton doesn't ripen all at once — you pick three, four times from September to October. Me and my husband can manage maybe the first round, but after that we hire women from the village. They get paid by the kilo, and it costs plenty, but what choice do we have? Two old people can't pick 10 mu by hand before the weather turns.

I expect about 250 kg of lint per mu if the weather is fair. Not more, not less. I'm too old for gambles. I need enough to live, to pay for the inputs, and maybe a little left for the winter. Steady is better than sorry.
